interactions.summary: Jiang answers Greg's invitation with his most extreme disclosure: he predicts 99 percent of humanity will die within a century through a cascading mix of geophysical upheaval, extreme weather, epidemics, war, and revolution.

Greg challenges the usefulness of apocalyptic prophecy by noting that many earlier seers saw catastrophe that never arrived within a human lifetime and asking whether timeline failure makes such visions practically useless.
Jiang replies that prophets perceive events without reliable timelines, so he uses short-term predictions as a live test of whether his own models or prophetic capacities deserve trust.

claims.claim: Jiang says he believes 99 percent of humanity will be wiped out in the next 100 years.
claims.temporal_scope: Explicit long-range prediction stated on 2025-10-07 about the next century.

claims.claim: Jiang says the mechanism is a perfect storm of crises including possible polar shift, mini ice age, destructive winter weather in North America, epidemics, wars, and revolutions.
claims.temporal_scope: Multi-cause apocalyptic scenario stated on 2025-10-07 covering the next 20 years and beyond.

claims.claim: Jiang says the coming 20 years resemble Kali Yuga, with no escape from worsening conditions.
claims.temporal_scope: Civilizational-spiritual prediction made on 2025-10-07 about the next two decades.

claims.claim: Greg says prophetic visions of catastrophe often fail to manifest on usable human timelines, making them difficult to apply practically even when cyclic collapse feels plausible.
claims.temporal_scope: Host critique posed on 2025-10-07 using examples from the 1980s and 1990s.

claims.claim: Jiang says prophets and mystics can see future events but not their timelines because higher consciousness does not perceive time and space the way ordinary human life does.

Jiang says he tests himself through short-term predictions such as the destruction of Al-Aqsa Mosque, a U.S. invasion of Iran, and NATO fighting Russia in Odessa; if they fail, listeners should regard him as a false prophet.
claims.temporal_scope: Present test framework stated on 2025-10-07 for near-future events.

claims.claim: Jiang says internet audiences are drawn to him because he appears to have predicted events and because the internet functions as a marketplace where predictions can be publicly tested.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang abruptly states that 99 percent of humanity will die within a century, turning the interview from edgy geopolitics into explicit apocalypse.
signature_moments.source_phrase: 99 % of humanity will be wiped out
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the single most explosive prediction in the interview and will define how readers interpret the rest of the prophetic material.

signature_moments.moment: His mechanism is not one clean disaster but a stacked storm of geophysical, epidemiological, military, and revolutionary shocks.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It shows the prediction is a compounded collapse model rather than a single-event prophecy.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang subjects mystical claims to a falsification test: if the short-term calls fail, listeners should write him off as a false prophet.
signature_moments.source_phrase: then you know i'm a false prophet
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It connects his prophetic register back to his predictive-history method and gives later readers a concrete verification frame.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang uses the term for an age of intensified breakdown in which the coming decades worsen relentlessly.
Jiang's own criterion for failure if his short-term predictions do not materialize.
Jiang's description of the internet as a place where predictions compete and can be judged by outcomes.

chronology_notes.note: This packet layers multiple time horizons: an extremely cold coming winter, a worsening 20-year crisis, a 50-year rebuilding horizon, and a 100-year mass-dieoff claim, then shifts back to near-term predictions as Jiang's test case.

uncertainty_notes.note: The mosque name in one prediction may be ASR-distorted and several cataclysm examples are speculative by nature, but the packet's core claims about timeline uncertainty and Jiang's self-testing method are clear.
